definition: On a flexible appendage (ears, cape, hair), the same inertial lag that causes drag/overlap/follow-through is often expressed not just as a rotational or positional delay but ALSO as a visible stretch along the direction of relative motion, since the appendage's base moves with the body while its tip resists.
purpose: Make a dragging appendage's lag read as a real physical consequence of the body's own motion (inertia acting on a flexible material) rather than as a separate, merely-delayed copy of the body's motion.
visible_effect: The appendage elongates along its own lag direction while dragging (e.g. a falling character's ears or cape stretching upward, opposite the fall direction), then compresses or relaxes back toward its rest length as it catches up and follows through.
psychological_or_gameplay_effect: Reads as the appendage RESISTING the body's motion (real inertia) rather than merely arriving late — the stretch is what makes the drag feel like a force acting on material, not just a timing offset.
physical_interpretation: An approximation of a flexible material's own inertia: the base accelerates with the body, the tip lags, and material connecting the two under tension visibly elongates in between — the same volume-preserving logic squash & stretch already states, applied here to explain WHY a dragging part often stretches rather than just lagging.
use_cases: a falling or fast-moving character with flexible trailing parts (ears, cape, hair, a tail) where the drag phase specifically should read as tension, not just delay
any moment the existing follow-through/overlap card already calls for drag, where squash & stretch is available as a style
non_use_cases: a rigid or mechanical trailing part (a rigid antenna, an armored plate) that should lag WITHOUT stretching
a realistic style where visible elongation would read as unnaturally elastic rather than merely delayed
interactions: Follow through & overlap — this names a concrete case of drag co-occurring with a SECOND principle rather than acting alone, on the same appendage at the same moment

Squash & stretch — the existing card's pose-based equivalent (`motion_amplitude`/`weight_transfer`) is the same lever this entry would need; the existing INTERACTION_GRAPH has no edge between `follow_through_overlap` and `squash_stretch` at all yet, though both individual cards exist — this entry is direct video evidence such an edge is warranted

style_variations.anime: may be exaggerated further than the source example
style_variations.mechanical: excluded — a rigid part should drag without stretching, same as squash & stretch's own mechanical exclusion

cadence_representation: Reachable only through the SAME pose-based route squash & stretch itself already uses, combined with `secondary_delay`'s existing lag mechanism: since Cadence has no mesh deformation, a literal stretch is unavailable, but `secondary_delay` (lag timing) plus `motion_amplitude`/`weight_transfer` (the pose-based equivalent of stretch) on the SAME trailing item's own rotation could jointly approximate the coupled effect this video shows — nothing currently coordinates the two dimensions together for this specific purpose.
control_surface: `secondary_delay` for the lag half; `motion_amplitude`/`weight_transfer` for the pose-based stretch-equivalent half; no tool currently applies both together as one declared technique.
detection_and_measurement_methods: `ai/motion.js analyseChain` measures the lag half directly; no scale/volume signal exists to measure an actual stretch (the same gap `squash_stretch`'s own card already states — no track in Cadence stores mesh scale over time).
generation_or_modification_methods: None jointly — the two halves would have to be authored as two separate dimension calls today, with no single control expressing the coupled technique.
failure_modes: authoring only the lag (`secondary_delay`) and skipping the pose-based stretch-equivalent, losing the tension read the source example relies on
applying visible stretch to a rigid/mechanical trailing part, which should drag without any stretch at all
roblox_considerations: A literal scale-based stretch IS representable in Roblox (Motor6D parts can be scaled), the same real, non-theoretical extension already named under `squash_stretch`'s own `roblox_considerations`.
performance_implications: None beyond the two existing dimensions' own costs, which are already accounted for.
examples: super bunny's ears explicitly stretching while dragging during a fall — "the ear should be stretching" — named as squash & stretch applied to the same drag moment (video @ 11:19–12:03)
the cape's edge described as starting to curve while part of it "is still dragging," a softer version of the same coupled effect (video @ 16:36–16:51)
evidence_status: video: https://youtu.be/t_gH-OADlSw @ 11:13–12:03 — Arree Chung states the squash-and-stretch-during-drag connection directly and explicitly in the transcript; a frame at t=11:46 in this session's sample shows the super-bunny figure with ears trailing at an angle during a fall pose, consistent with but not sharp enough to confirm an actual stretched (elongated) ear shape; experimental until validated
